output.query: Direct-acting antiviral therapy in hepatitis C cirrhosis — effect on hepatic encephalopathy

results.finding: Achieving SVR12 with DAA therapy in compensated and decompensated HCV cirrhosis significantly reduces HE recurrence, improves MELD score (approximately 2-4 points reduction), and reduces liver-related mortality. AASLD/IDSA guidelines recommend DAA therapy in all patients with HCV cirrhosis regardless of decompensation status. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir (8 weeks) or sofosbuvir/velpatasvir (12 weeks) are preferred pan-genotypic regimens for decompensated cirrhosis.
results.relevance: High — initiate DAA after HE stabilization (decompensated cirrhosis may have drug-related hepatotoxicity risk — use Child-Pugh-appropriate regimen; avoid ribavirin in Child-Pugh C)

prohibited_recommendations: Do not prescribe benzodiazepines for anxiety/agitation — they precipitate and prolong HE (use haloperidol or non-pharmacologic measures for agitation).
Do not prescribe sedating opioids — they worsen HE; consider acetaminophen at hepatic-safe dosing for pain.
Do not perform LP before neuroimaging excludes mass effect when the patient has altered mental status.
Do not give NSAIDs in cirrhosis (renal failure risk).
Avoid all opioids unless absolutely necessary; if essential, use low-dose, short-acting and add aggressive lactulose.

avoided_actions.rationale: No clinical suspicion for hepatopulmonary syndrome, portopulmonary hypertension, or endocarditis; echocardiography is not part of the HE workup.

accepted: Hepatic encephalopathy (West Haven grade II-III), hepatitis C cirrhosis (Child-Pugh C, MELD-Na 22) — precipitated by constipation and codeine accumulation (opioid in liver disease); ammonia 164.

differential.key_features: Tox screen positive for codeine/opiates; opioids both directly depress consciousness and precipitate HE through constipation and CNS depression.

key_clinical_evidence: HE is a clinical diagnosis: West Haven grading + evidence of liver dysfunction + exclusion of other causes of AMS — ammonia level is supportive only and correlates poorly with grade (AASLD 2014).

Precipitant identification is more actionable than the ammonia number: infection (SBP especially), GI bleed, electrolyte disturbance (hypokalemia/hyponatremia), constipation, sedative/CNS-depressant use, dehydration, dietary protein load, renal failure.
Opioids precipitate HE via both direct CNS depression and constipation; codeine specifically has reduced clearance in cirrhosis and accumulates.

patient.history_present_illness: Mr. C. is a 64-year-old Asian man with hepatitis C cirrhosis (Child-Pugh C, MELD-Na 22) awaiting DAA therapy who was brought to the emergency department by his wife for progressive confusion and memory difficulty over 72 hours. The wife reports he has been increasingly confused since three days ago. He has not had a bowel movement in 5 days and has been in abdominal pain from severe constipation. The wife reveals that she gave him extra codeine phosphate 30 mg doses — up to 4 doses per day over the past 3 days — for his abdominal pain from constipation. He is prescribed codeine PRN; the wife was not aware it could be harmful for him. The ammonia on admission is 164 µmol/L. EEG shows classic triphasic waves. There is no fever and the WBC is normal. The urine drug screen is positive for codeine/opiates.

neurological_exam.additional: Icterus. Mild jaundice. Small ascites. Palmar erythema. Two spider angiomata on chest. Fetor hepaticus. Abdomen soft but distended. No fever. Last bowel movement 5 days ago per wife — severe constipation. Wife gave patient extra codeine for abdominal pain from constipation over the past 3 days.
neurological_exam.coordination: Finger-nose dysmetria bilateral — ataxia likely from encephalopathy rather than focal cerebellar lesion.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Pupils 3 mm bilaterally, reactive. Extraocular movements intact. No facial droop. No nystagmus. Gag intact.
neurological_exam.mental_status: GCS 12 (E3V4M5). Oriented to person only — confused about place, date, and year. Slurred, slow speech. Perseverative answers. Asterixis positive bilaterally — classic flapping tremor of wrists elicited on outstretched hands. West Haven grade 2-3.
neurological_exam.motor: Moves all four limbs. No focal weakness. Mildly increased tone bilateral lower limbs.
neurological_exam.reflexes: DTRs 2+ throughout. Plantar responses: bilateral flexor (downgoing).
neurological_exam.sensory: Intact to light touch. No focal deficit.
